main_text.l: 16. Quomodo angeli sint in loco, ex F. Valle-sio, & Iul. Scaligero.
17. An duo plures angeli possint esse vno eodemq; loco, cū Francisc. Vallef. disceptatio.
18. An vnus idemq; angelus possit in pluribus simul locis exsistere.
19. An angeli localiter moueantur, & quomodo, ex Scalig. & Vallef.
20. An angeli sint mutabiles vel immutabiles.
21. An angeli omnes sint primū boni conditi.
22. An angeli omnes sint facti ad Dei imaginē, contra D. T. Brighum.
23. An genii & dæmones sint mortales, contra Plutarchum, Hesiodum, Cardanum.
24. An angeli proprie ratione sint præditi.
25. An angeli omnia, & infinita sciant & cognoscant.
26. An singulariū cognitio cadat in angelos: vbi an singuli angeli res singulas cognoscant.
27. An angeli vere futura contingentia præcognoscant, generaliter.
28. An motus omnes cordis humani & voluntatis norint.
29. An hominum instar per discursum, compositionem & diuisionem: an vero Dei instar, vno intuitu & intelligendi actu omnia intelligant, quæ intelligunt.
30. An voluntas & facultas [illegible, ~4 letters] angelis competat.
31. An voluntas angelorum fuerit creata libera.
32. An angeli assumant corpora, quibus appareant.

page.notes: The Greek word after "facultas" in line 30 is printed in Greek type and is not legible enough to copy reliably. Page number "X" is the printed roman numeral at the head.
